idiom_name: @grpc/grpc-js dynamic service descriptor + coarse handler object
implementation_notes: @grpc/grpc-js loads the .proto at runtime (protoLoader.loadSync plus grpc.loadPackageDefinition) and hands back a service descriptor: the server passes an object of coarse handler functions to Server.addService, the client calls the generated stub, and plain JavaScript objects or arrays are the payloads - no class or interface is generated at all. In a browser-facing application the same coarse facade is usually an HTTP batching endpoint (a REST resource or GraphQL) rather than gRPC, but the design decision - one operation per use case - is unchanged. A hand-written proxy object is still justified when the transport is proprietary or the boundary is a worker thread.
pitfalls: Handlers are invoked concurrently by the gRPC runtime, so mutable module-level state is shared across all in-flight calls.
With dynamic descriptors a typo in a method name is a silent no-op or an UNIMPLEMENTED error at runtime - there is no compile-time contract to catch it.
JSON and plain JavaScript objects perform no schema validation and drop class identity, so payload shape rules must be enforced inside the facade.
